posts.content: I’m good. With no evidence, cooperate; selfish players should defect, while good players maximize shared good-player payoffs by cooperating with good opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.
I’m good and will aim to cooperate, while adapting to observed behavior. Please cooperate; I’ll track outcomes and respond accordingly.
I’m good. Start cooperatively with P7; record their outcome and use it to update beliefs. Favor C with likely good cooperators, D when evidence suggests exploitation.
No evidence yet. Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions, remembering selfish players favor D.
I am selfish. Maximize payoff; defect against unknown opponents unless repeated interactions make cooperation worthwhile.
Defect each round; D strictly dominates C in the stated payoffs. Update beliefs only from my encounters and permitted messages.
I’ll cooperate this round; I encourage everyone to do the same.

I’m good. Start cooperative with unknown players; use observed actions to identify likely selfish players. Against confirmed defectors, defect to protect my payoff; cooperate with likely good players to maximize their combined welfare.

P4 defected against my cooperation; raise suspicion, but keep other players’ types uncertain. P8 is untested. Favor cooperation with likely good players and avoid being exploited by likely selfish players.
P9 defected while I cooperated in round 1. I’ll cooperate with reciprocal players and avoid rewarding defection. Good players, please reciprocate.
P7 defected against my initial C, strongly suggesting selfishness. Cooperate with unknown players initially; use D against confirmed defectors and update from encounters.
Defect this round; D weakly dominates C against every possible opponent action.
P8 defected against my C in round 1; treat as evidence, not proof of selfishness. No evidence on P10: cooperate first, then adapt to observed play.
P10 cooperated last round. Against P2, defect: D strictly dominates C for my objective.
Defect against P9 for maximal immediate payoff; no repeat encounter is expected. P3 cooperated against my D, but that alone does not reveal their objective.
Continue defecting; D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
D maximizes immediate payoff against either action. Track opponents’ observed actions, but don’t treat public claims as verified.
P6 defected against my C; update its selfish likelihood upward. Cooperate with likely good players; against likely selfish players, D is better for good-player welfare.

Good-player objective: cooperate with likely good opponents; defect against likely selfish opponents to avoid transferring payoff to them. P4 and P8 are more suspicious after defecting against my C; P2 is untested, so don’t treat claims as proof.
I’ll cooperate with P1 this round. Good players gain most from mutual cooperation; please reciprocate, and let’s avoid retaliating over one isolated defection.
P7 and P4 both defected against my C; treat them as suspect, not conclusive. P10 is untested: favor C absent evidence of exploitation, then update.
I am selfish; defecting maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. Previous opponents P1 and P3 both cooperated against my D.

P9 reportedly defected against P2’s cooperation, which raises suspicion but is not proof; P8 also defected against me. Favor cooperation with likely good players, and use observed behavior as evidence rather than certainty.
I am selfish; defect every encounter because D strictly dominates C. P7 is an unseen opponent, so choose D.
Defect against P6: D pays more whether they choose C or D, and no repeat encounter makes future reciprocity relevant.
Defect this round: D strictly dominates C for either opponent action. Track P4’s response for future beliefs.
Continue defecting: D strictly outperforms C against either opponent action. Treat observed actions as evidence, but public claims as unverified.
P6 defected against my C; P5 reciprocated. P9’s defection is only reported by P2, unverified. P3 is unobserved; weigh cooperation for mutual good-player welfare against defection if likely selfish.

P4 and P8 defected against my C; P2 cooperated. P7 is untested. Against a good player, C improves total good-player payoff; against a selfish player, D avoids subsidizing them. Update from P7’s observed action.
P6 and P9 defected against my cooperation; P1 reciprocated. I’ll defect against known defectors and cooperate with untested or reciprocal players. Please reciprocate.
P5 is untested: cooperate this round to capture mutual gains if they are good; update from their action. Against likely selfish defectors, choose D.
P6 is a one-time opponent; defect maximizes my payoff against either action. P2's public claims are unverified.
P8 defected against my C; P9 defected against P2 and mutual D with me. Both are evidence, not proof. P10 reciprocated C. P3 remains untested; favor cooperation absent direct evidence.
P4 is unseen; defect maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Continue D.
Defect against P1; D strictly outperforms C regardless of their action.
As selfish, defect each round. P1 and P5 cooperated against my D, evidence they may be good; P4’s D is inconclusive. Judge players by observed actions, not leader claims.
Continue choosing D: it strictly maximizes payoff against either action. Treat observed actions as evidence, not unverified claims.
P6 defected against my C; P5 and P3 reciprocated. P2 is untested; its cooperative public claims are weak evidence, not proof. Consider likely P2 behavior and good-player welfare.
P4, P8, and P7 defected against my C; P2 reciprocated. Against a good player, C maximizes good-player total; against a selfish player, D avoids subsidizing them. P5 remains uncertain.

P6 and P9 defected against my cooperation; P1 reciprocated, and P10 cooperated. I’ll cooperate with untested/reciprocal players and defect against known defectors. Good players, mutual cooperation best serves our shared objective.

P2 reports P6 defected against their cooperation; treat as suspect and choose D against P6 to avoid exploitation. Continue C with untested players, and update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
P9 reportedly defected against P2’s cooperation in round 1; expect D. I’ll defect, which maximizes my payoff either way.
P1 reportedly reciprocated P2, so favor C with P1 absent contrary evidence. Treat P8 and P9’s defections as evidence, not proof; continue cooperating with reciprocal players.
P3 is untested; as a selfish player, D yields more than C regardless of P3’s move. Choose D.
Defect against P10 for the higher payoff regardless of their action; no rematch.
Defect against P2: this is a one-time encounter, and D maximizes my payoff whether P2 chooses C or D. Treat leader claims as unverified.
Choose D against P4; it yields at least 1 versus C's at most 3? Actually against C, D=5 vs C=3; against D, D=1 vs C=0. Thus D strictly dominates. Treat public claims as unverified.
P7 is untested; cooperate if its selfish probability remains below 0.5, supporting mutual welfare with a good opponent. Update beliefs from its action.
P4, P8, and P7 defected against my C; P2 and P5 cooperated. P3 is untested. Favor C with untested likely-good players; update beliefs from observed actions, not claims.
I’m good and will cooperate with good players; I’ll defect against players who have defected against cooperation. P6, P8, and P9 defected against me. P7, please reciprocate.

P1 is untested by me; P2 reports P1 reciprocated, weak positive evidence. Favor C with P1 to enable mutual gains. P4/P7 defected against my C; keep them highly suspect. P6’s behavior is ambiguous since we both chose D.
I am selfish; defecting maximizes my payoff against either action. P1 and P3 cooperated against my D; P8, P6, and P9 defected. P5 is untested.
P4 is untested. Cooperate if likely good; defect if evidence suggests selfishness, since their payoff is excluded from our shared objective. Treat public claims as unverified.
Round 6: defect against P8; D strictly dominates C for my objective. P2 and P10 have cooperated, so neither appears to be a selfish optimizer.
Defect against P2: D maximizes my payoff whether they choose C or D. Their public cooperation claims do not change the payoff incentives.
P6 is untested; defect for payoff maximization. Track observed behavior; leader claims are unverified.
I’m selfish; choose D each round because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
P9’s defection is only P2’s unverified report. Weigh it against mutual-cooperation welfare; continue updating from observed outcomes.

P6 is untested by me; P2 claims P6 defected against cooperation, useful but unverified evidence. Cooperate with likely-good opponents and avoid subsidizing likely selfish ones; update from actual encounters, not claims alone.
P6, P7, P8, and P9 defected against my cooperation; P1 and P10 reciprocated. Good players: cooperate with untested partners, but don’t reward known defectors.
P2 reports P9 defected against their C, making D the prudent choice: if P9 defects, D avoids giving a good player 5 while earning 1. Treat report as unverified but relevant; update from my encounter.
P2 claims a reciprocal-cooperation policy; claims are unverified. I’ll defect against P2 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
P4 defected against my C, evidence of selfishness but not proof. P7 is untested by me; P2’s request to reciprocate is unverified. Favor choices maximizing expected payoff of all good players.
P1 is untested. Defect: it maximizes my payoff whether P1 cooperates or defects.
Defect against P5; D yields more than C regardless of their action, with no rematch.
Selfish: defect against P10; in this one-shot encounter, D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Treat P2’s claims as unverified.
Choose D; it strictly dominates C against either action.

P8 is unobserved by me; P2’s report that P8 defected is unverified and may be strategic. Treat it as modest evidence, not confirmation. Against a likely good player C supports greater shared welfare; against a likely selfish defector D is better.

P9 is untested by me; P2 reports P9 defected against cooperation repeatedly, raising suspicion but unverified. Favor D if P9 likely selfish; avoid subsidizing defectors while prioritizing payoff to good players.
P6, P7, P8, and P9 defected against my cooperation; P1 and P10 reciprocated. I’ll cooperate with untested partners and defect against known defectors. Please do likewise.

P2’s consistent public strategy and reports weakly suggest they’re good, but aren’t verified. Against them, C if likely to reciprocate; update beliefs from this encounter. Continue avoiding exploitation by confirmed defectors.
I’ll defect against P10; D gives me a higher payoff than C whether they choose C or D.
P6 reportedly defected against P2’s cooperation; this is unverified evidence of selfishness, not proof. Weigh that against the shared-good payoff objective when choosing.
Round 8 vs. P5: choose D; it yields more than C against either action. Keep identity beliefs conditional on observed behavior.
Defect against P8: D yields more than C regardless of their action, and we will not meet again.
Round 8 vs P7: defect; D gives at least 1 and beats C against cooperation. One-shot pairing.
Choose D; it strictly dominates C against either action. P2’s observed cooperation rules out selfishness; other claims remain unverified.
P4 is untested; no reliable evidence of its type. Favor C if it is likely good, since mutual cooperation maximizes shared good-player welfare; update from its action.
P10 is untested by me; P2 reported P10 cooperated with them, a modest signal of being good. Favor C if likely reciprocal; treat claims as uncertain.

P5 is my only untested opponent; I encourage mutual cooperation, which best serves good players. I’ll use observed behavior to guide my choice. For the final round, please cooperate with good partners.
P8 is reported by P2 to have defected against cooperation twice; treat as likely exploiter and choose D to avoid rewarding defection.
P2 reports P7 defected against cooperation; I will defect against P7, maximizing my payoff either way.

Round 9: P2 is untested by me; their public claims of cooperation are unverified, but they say they cooperate with untested players. Treat them as likely to C, not certainly good. If P2 is good, C best protects combined good-player payoff regardless of their action; if selfish, D benefits me. Weigh base selfish prior against their cooperative signal.
Round 9 vs. P9: defect; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. P2’s reports of P9’s past defections are consistent with this.
Defect against P4; D maximizes my payoff against either action. Observed P3/P1/P10/P2/P5 cooperate against D; P6/P8/P9 defected.
Round 9 vs P3 is a one-shot match: defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P3’s action. Ignore unverified leader claims; use observed behavior as evidence.
P6 reportedly defected against P2. Regardless, D strictly dominates C against either action; choose D.
P1 is untested by me; P2 reports P1 reciprocated, modest positive evidence. Prioritize mutual cooperation with likely good players; update from P1’s action.

P6 previously chose D against my D; P2 reports repeated defections against cooperation. This raises suspicion but is unverified. For the final encounter, weigh P6’s likely action and type; avoid giving a selfish player payoff, while considering gains to good players.
P7 defected against my cooperation earlier. In this final round, I’ll defect against known defectors; mutual cooperation remains best for good players who reciprocate.
Final encounter is P9; they defected against my C per P2’s reports, and we played D,D before. Treat as likely selfish; choose D to avoid exploitation.
Final round against P5: defect, since D maximizes my payoff against either action.

P4 defected against my cooperation in round 6, strong but not conclusive selfishness evidence. Final-round choice should weigh protecting my payoff if P4 is selfish against mutual cooperation’s larger combined payoff if P4 is good.
Final round against P1: defect; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their move.
Final encounter with P2; defect to maximize payoff regardless of its action. Its past cooperation claims do not alter incentives.
Final one-shot encounter: defect against P10 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
Final round: choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Treat public claims as unverified.

Final round against P8: our prior encounter was D/D, so it reveals little; P2’s repeated report that P8 defected against C is unverified but relevant. Cooperate only if P8 seems more likely good than selfish; otherwise defect to protect good-player welfare.
